data.title: Anti-Disassembly Tricks
data.summary: The binary contains code deliberately crafted to desynchronise a disassembler's instruction boundaries — overlapping instructions, jumps into the middle of another instruction's bytes — producing a garbage listing around the real logic.
data.description:
This targets the disassembler specifically, rather than the analyst's time generally: a
jump target that lands one byte into what looks like a different instruction causes most
linear disassemblers to decode the wrong instruction stream from that point, hiding the
real control flow in what the tool reports as nonsense or as a different, misleading
instruction sequence entirely.
data.recommendation:
* Switch to a recursive-traversal disassembler or correct the desynchronisation by hand at the known jump target before trusting the listing.
* Verify disassembly against a dynamic instruction trace at the affected offset rather than the static listing alone.
* Note the exact offset and technique; it is cheap for the analyst to correct once found but easy to miss on a first pass.
data.short_recommendation: Verify the affected offset against a dynamic instruction trace rather than trusting static disassembly there.

mitre_techniques.procedure: A jump landed mid-instruction, desynchronising the static disassembly from the actual executed instruction stream.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Overlapping instruction encoding at a jump target desynchronised linear disassembly.
